activities.anchor: spread wider and compress bond angles
activities.caption: set water's bond angle where the lone pairs leave it
activities.name: cmdWaterPlace

config.prompt: Methane's tetrahedron sits at 109.5°. Water has two bonds plus two lone pairs — place its H–O–H angle on the scale:
config.why: 104.5°: lone pairs spread wider than bonding pairs and squeeze the angle — geometry from a two-dimensional count, the translation VSEPR licenses.

activities.anchor: a one-letter code for its local dimensionality
activities.caption: pair each orbital construct with its signature
activities.name: cmdHybridMatch

config.prompt: From sketches to quantum mechanics — pair each construct with what it explains:

pairs.right: four equivalent lobes pointing tetrahedrally — carbon in diamond and methane
three planar lobes plus a perpendicular p orbital — graphene and benzene's delocalised rings
the Lewis structure cannot explain the paramagnetism; filling MOs from the bottom predicts it

config.why: Read the hybrid, know the geometry — and the same formalism, scaled to ~10²³ orbitals smeared into bands, yields the band gap: the most computed number in the field.

activities.anchor: docking scores live or die on them
activities.caption: file each soft interaction with its family
activities.name: cmdForcesBuckets

config.prompt: Three weak forces organise matter — file each fact:

items.label: instantaneous dipoles from fluctuating electron clouds — present everywhere
a gecko's climb, multiplied over billions of nanoscale contacts
H bonded to N, O or F, attracted to a lone pair
worth roughly 10–40 kJ/mol against covalent bonds' 150–1,000

config.why: The magnitudes are the design information — water boils 180 degrees above its weight class, DNA unzips one base at a time, and nacre's toughness lives at interfaces.

activities.anchor: the way a machinist knows the machine
activities.caption: rebuild DFT's bargain, step by step
activities.name: cmdDftOrder

config.prompt: From hopeless exactness to engineering prediction — drag the bargain into order:
items: Brute force dies first: 10 interacting electrons already exceed any conceivable memory
Hohenberg–Kohn (1964): the ground-state electron density determines everything about the system
Kohn–Sham (1965): swap the interacting problem for non-interacting electrons in an approximate potential
The payoff: lattice constants within a few percent, formation energies, elastic moduli, band structures
The craft: know the blind spots — band gaps underestimated, dispersion patched, DFT+U for correlated oxides
config.why: Nobel 1998 (Kohn with Pople). The practitioner knows the error bars the way a machinist knows the machine's backlash.

activities.caption: call the size of GNoME's stability frontier
activities.name: cmdGnomeEstimate

config.prompt: DeepMind's GNoME (2023) proposed 2.2 million new crystal structures. Roughly how many sit on the computed stability frontier?
config.why: About 380,000 — multiplying the roughly 48,000 stable inorganic crystals known from a century of experiment several times over, in one publication.
config.context: The caveat that keeps the field honest: surrogates interpolate well and extrapolate poorly — training-set coverage bounds trust.

activities.caption: bet the A-Lab scoreboard before the reveal
activities.name: cmdAlabPredict

config.q: In its 2023 run, the Berkeley A-Lab autonomously proposed and tried to make 58 crystals over 17 days. How many formed?
choices: 41 — an extraordinary rate for new materials, with a miss rate no serious loop pretends away
0 — predicted compounds always fail to synthesise
3 — synthesis is the bottleneck that never yields
config.why: 41 of 58: metastability, competing phases and kinetic barriers that a 0-kelvin ground-state calculation never sees. Computation narrows the funnel; the furnace still gets the final word.

activities.caption: walk the self-driving laboratory's next move
activities.name: cmdLoopBranch

config.root: Design–make–test once cost a PhD student a year. You are running the compressed loop.

start.text: The robot line is idle and the algorithm must choose the next sample. Which policy do you run?

choices.label: Bayesian optimisation — pick the experiment that maximises information
choices.feedback: The steepest knowledge-per-sample curve is the whole point of closing the loop.

choices.label: Forward screening — propose, compute, filter the top candidates
choices.feedback: The classic funnel. Inverse design runs it the other way round.

choices.label: Trust the surrogate even at the extrapolation edge
choices.feedback: Where the training data ends, the model guesses.

info.text: Active learning chooses the sample that teaches the model most — the design–make–test cycle learns where to look next instead of waiting for luck. High-entropy alloys and solid-state electrolytes came out of loops like this.

forward.text: Forward screening sweeps a candidate space and filters. Inverse design inverts it: specify the property — a target band gap, a modulus — and search structure space for what delivers it.

blind.text: Surrogates interpolate within their training manifolds and inherit their biases; several prominent database entries failed independent reproduction. Outside the manifold, only synthesis and measurement decide what is real.

config.why: The MGI's 2011 premise — halve discovery-to-deployment by making computation first-class — has largely been met; the bottleneck moved to data quality, robotics and judgement.

activities.anchor: still needed synthesis to exist and measurement to be believed
activities.caption: true or false — the division of labour, audited
activities.name: cmdVerifyJudge

statements.s: Machine learning has made experiments optional — the surrogate's word is the result.
statements.why: Models interpolate within their training manifolds and inherit their biases; the strongest predictions remain hypotheses until a furnace agrees.

statements.s: Several prominent database entries failed independent reproduction.
statements.why: Which is why standard benchmarks and uncertainty-quantified models are the frontier responses.

statements.s: Computation narrows a candidate space by orders of magnitude; experiments decide what is real.
statements.why: The accurate division of labour — search is automated, verification is not.

statements.s: Negative results — compounds that failed to synthesise — are archived as carefully as successes.
statements.why: They are barely archived anywhere, and DFT's systematic errors become the surrogate's priors.
